notes:
This is an early build, released to consoles set to Latest Updates.

The Wind Waker HD can now run as a native port, built on your console from your own
copy of the game: the USA or European version 0, as a Cemu archive (.wua) or a game
folder. Its tile is in Ports and Apps. On the web page, open Ports and Apps, then The
Wind Waker HD, add your .wua there (a copy already in your Wii U library works too)
and press Build. The build takes about 40 minutes, then the tile plays the game, at
30 fps on Outset Island. Hold Minus in the game for its settings. It keeps its own
saves, so your Wii U emulator saves do not carry over yet.

Wii U games use less of the processor. The emulator's graphics thread used to keep a
whole processor core busy while it waited for work; it now rests between frames. Wind
Waker HD in the Wii U emulator uses about half a core less at the same frame rate,
which means less heat and battery drain, and Star Fox Zero runs slightly faster.

Loading a PS2 save state no longer ejects the memory card just because the game saved
since: games that overwrite their save, like Jak II with its auto-save, no longer say
the card was removed. A state still ejects the card when a save was created, deleted
or changed size since the state was made, which protects the saves on it. Save states
made before this update behave as before.

The Wind Waker HD port was tested handheld on Outset Island; docked play, sailing and
long sessions have not been tried. The Wii U emulator sometimes closes itself in the
first seconds of a game, about 1 in 5 Wind Waker HD starts in testing, before this
update as well; start the game again. The PS2 memory card fix was tested with Jak II.

stable.notes:
The 2.41 changes, now on the Stable channel. If this console was on 2.40.0,
it also gets the whole 2.40 series, summed up at the end.

This update carries a new boot script: the console restarts once for the
update and once more on its own about a minute after the first boot. Do not
power off while it says part 2 of 2.

The SD card's fastest mode (DDR200) is now used on Samsung cards only, as
Switchroot does. Other cards run in the standard mode: if yours used the
fast mode, games load a little slower, but SanDisk cards, which cannot run
it reliably on the Switch, no longer get read errors under load. If a
Samsung card gives read errors, turn DDR200 off in the SCCM Retro app's Boot
settings.

The SCCM Retro app on the Homebrew menu is now one app: Launch SCCM Retro,
Launch in Safe Mode (stock clocks and voltages, once), Options (WiFi and
Bluetooth, boot settings, auto launch), and installing or removing SCCM
Retro on an SD card. The separate installer and calibration apps are
removed.

Swap A and B now applies only to Gen1Recomp and Moonlight, the two games
that offer it.

New background: Arcade, in Settings, Display and Sound, Appearance.

From 2.40.0, also: the console boots in about 28 seconds instead of about
50; Ocarina of Time and Majora's Mask, and Mario Kart Wii as a native port
with Retro Rewind online, on Ports and Apps; a PC Games tab for Windows
games; auto save for RetroArch, 3DS and PS2 games; Wii U, GameCube, WiFi
and volume button fixes; and a security fix to install permissions.
